package_info.why_malicious: The package is malicious because it establishes a persistent, encrypted two-way communication channel with a remote C2 server upon installation, exfiltrates host and machine identifiers, and executes attacker-supplied, encrypted JavaScript payloads on the victim's machine. The package uses obfuscation, background daemonization, and anti-analysis techniques to evade detection and enable remote code execution.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the code executes index.js automatically upon package installation, launching the malicious payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automatically executing code on install is a common malware technique to ensure immediate execution without user interaction.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely require postinstall scripts unless for build or setup; here, it is used to trigger malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages use postinstall for compiling native modules or setup tasks.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the code uses pm2 to launch app.js as a persistent, background daemon in cluster mode, ensuring the malicious process remains running.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Spawning a background daemon on install is highly unusual and enables persistent malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not install persistent background processes on developer machines.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: pm2 is used legitimately to manage Node.js services in production, but not during package installation.
key_indicators: pm2 used to daemonize a script at install time

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code dynamically generates an AES encryption key and a C2 server URL using obfuscated logic, making static analysis and detection more difficult.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated generation of keys and URLs is a hallmark of malware attempting to evade detection and analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not obfuscate static configuration like keys or URLs.
key_indicators: dynamic C2 URL and key generation

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Every 45 seconds at runtime, the code collects host and machine identifiers, encrypts them, and sends them to the C2 server. It then receives an encrypted payload, decodes and executes it using eval, enabling remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Periodic exfiltration of host info and execution of remote, attacker-supplied code is highly malicious and enables full compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not beacon to remote servers or execute arbitrary code from the network.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (daemonized by pm2, on first run)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks for a marker file (node_logs.txt) in the temp directory. If absent, it creates the file and starts the heartbeat communication loop, acting as a one-time execution token.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of a marker file to control execution flow is a stealth technique to avoid repeated execution and detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not use hidden marker files to control malicious logic.
key_indicators: hidden marker file in temp directory
conditional execution based on file presence

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code encrypts all outbound and inbound C2 communications using AES-128-CBC, making network traffic analysis and detection more difficult.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Custom encryption of C2 traffic is a strong indicator of malware attempting to evade network-based detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely encrypt their own network traffic with custom keys and algorithms.

attack_chain.action: Upon installation, the postinstall script executes index.js.
index.js uses pm2 to launch app.js as a persistent background daemon.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious logic in app.js

attack_chain.action: app.js checks for a marker file and, if absent, creates it and starts the heartbeat loop.
Every 45 seconds, heartbeat collects host info and sends it (encrypted) to the C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: C2 server can respond with encrypted payloads

attack_chain.action: If a payload is received, it is decrypted, base64-decoded, and executed via eval, enabling remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker achieves arbitrary code execution on victim machine

behavioral_signatures: postinstall script executing custom Node.js code
pm2 used to daemonize scripts during package installation
periodic (e.g., every 45 seconds) outbound HTTPS POST requests to hardcoded or obfuscated C2 domains
eval execution of decrypted, network-supplied JavaScript
file_indicators: Presence of node_logs.txt in system temp directory
Obfuscated or unusually large app.js file with benign exports and hidden malicious logic
index.js that only launches pm2 with app.js
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to ql.rustdesk.net or 62.234.32.226
User-Agent string: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/103.0.5060.134
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with postinstall scripts that launch pm2 or background daemons. Flag packages that create marker files in temp directories (e.g., node_logs.txt) and those that make periodic outbound HTTPS POST requests to suspicious or obfuscated domains, especially with encrypted payloads. Detect use of eval on decrypted network data. Analyze app.js files for obfuscated code and hidden logic at the end of otherwise benign files.
